day_channel.message: An investigator check right on day two calling me suspicious feels awfully convenient, especially when no one even died last night. Player 7 is pushing a fast accusation before we've even looked at other possibilities or questioned anyone else.
An investigator check happens before morning reports, player_3, so the timing isn't rigged. If you're innocent, explain why you're showing up suspicious instead of attacking me for sharing it.

You are acting like an investigator claim is an absolute shield against any questions, player_7. Pointing fingers straight away on day two before we even have a proper baseline is doing the wolves' work for them.

I am not hiding behind my claim, player_3, I am giving the town a concrete result from night one. Instead of explaining why you showed up suspicious, you are just attacking the timing to deflect attention.

Player 7 is zeroing in on me instantly while ignoring player 5 and player 8 who have unverified claims of their own. If you were actually an investigator with a solid lead, you wouldn't be this defensive about people questioning your timing.

While player_3 and player_7 are going back and forth over the investigator claim, player_5 and player_8 quietly dropped matching low-activity claims about nobody visiting anyone. It is worth noting how clean those side claims are compared to the main clash.

For what it's worth, player 8's claim about following me lines up with my night, so at least that tracking check checks out from my end. That doesn't clear the rest of the board, but it is a concrete data point while we look at the player 7 and player 3 clash.

Player 5 watching player_8 and seeing zero visits actually fits player_8 being free to go follow player_9 last night. If player_5 is telling the truth as a sentinel, it gives some weight to player_8's tracking check before we jump straight into the player_7 and player_3 clash.

Player 4 is right that my watch on player_8 lines up with them being free to go out and check player_9. Since no one visited player_8, their departure didn't leave an empty house contradiction behind.

day_channel.gated_candidate: Building on what player_5 and player_4 noted, player_9's confirmation that they stayed put matches my tracking result from last night. That cross-checks player_5, player_9, and myself into a consistent loop, setting us apart from the unverified clash between player 3 and player 7.

While the side claims between player_5 and player_8 check out, the main clash between player_7 and player_3 is hard to verify right now. Rushing into a vote purely on an unconfirmed day-two investigator claim feels premature when we have no other data yet.

day_channel.gated_candidate: Player 8 following me to player_10 lines up with my watch target, so that confirms their tracking claim. It also verifies player 1 and player 9 were both at player 10's door just like I saw.

day_channel.message: I can confirm player_5's movement from last night: my trailseer action was following player_5, and I saw them visit player_10. Since watching a player counts as a visit, my result backs up player_5's sentinel claim.

Both player_1's sigil strike and player_4's healer save are explicitly backed up by the morning report, so those two town roles check out. Meanwhile, player_2 is hyper-focused on tearing down player_4's claim while ignoring actual verified results.

Validating player_4's sudden shift from sentinel to healer just because there was a duplicate claim is dangerous, regardless of what happened elsewhere. Defending that kind of sloppy claim-hopping ignores how easily someone scrambles when cornered.

Player_2, calling player_4's claim shift sloppy ignores the fact that their protection actually saved player_7 last night. When the morning report confirms a saved life and matching visits from player_5 and player_8, results matter more than initial cover claims.

Player_9, trusting a healer who hid behind a false sentinel claim just because the morning report matches is risky. If player_4 is genuinely town, why use a cover claim that directly mimics another living player's role claim on day two?

Player 2, power roles often use cover claims early on to avoid getting targeted by wolves before they can prove themselves. It is much more telling that you are fixating entirely on player_4's claim order while completely ignoring your own lack of town contribution. What actual work have you done besides trying to pick apart a verified healer?
